$schema-note: The single source of truth for both store listings (FR-088). Read by apps/mobile/app.config.ts in Node at prebuild time, by listing/scripts/verify-listing.mjs as a gate, and by a person preparing a submission (listing/submission.md). JSON because those three consumers have nothing else in common — research D1.
$what-lives-here: claims are store-independent facts about the app. stores.* are one store's rendering of those facts into its own fields, bounded by listing/limits.json. Nothing here is bundled or present at runtime on any platform.

claims.purposeSentence: Chromatic Tuner listens to your instrument to show which note you are playing. Audio is analysed entirely on this device and is never recorded, stored, or sent anywhere.
claims.price: Free, with no in-app purchases and no advertising.
claims.requirements: A microphone, and nothing else. After the first load it works with no network connection at all.
claims.$identifier-note: Permanent from first publication — neither store permits changing it afterwards (D3, FR-106). Chosen over com.prielaidas.chromatictuner because the Android package is the half a user sees, in the Play Store URL that gets pasted into a chat.
claims.$appName-note: One form, with the space, across the home-screen label, the microphone prompt, both listings, and apps/web/src/content.ts. app.json used to say ChromaticTuner while the web said Chromatic Tuner; FR-105 requires the prompt, the listing copy, and the privacy policy to explain the same purpose in the same terms, and two names for one product is where that starts to fail. Decided 2026-08-05.
claims.$collectsNoData-note: True because the app makes no network requests during use (FR-030), which apps/web/e2e/no-network.spec.ts asserts. FR-103 binds the store privacy declaration to that check rather than to a promise: adding analytics, crash reporting, or an update ping turns that gate red and makes this field false in the same commit.
claims.$corroboration-note: Each claim restated as the concept a reader must be able to take away, with the phrasings that count as saying it. L6 requires every concept to appear in both stores' copy; L7 requires every concept to appear in the rendered text of the built web page. Concepts rather than sentences, because the two stores' field structures differ by design (spec edge case 1) — byte comparison would either fail always or force copy that wastes one store's fields. Adding a claim to a listing means adding it here, which means the web page has to say it too.

ios.name: Guitar Tuner: Chromatic
ios.subtitle: Free, accurate, offline
ios.promotionalText: Pluck one string and see the note you are playing and how far off it is, to within a single cent. It keeps working with no network at all, so it is there in any room.
ios.description:
Chromatic Tuner is a free guitar tuner. Allow it to use your microphone, pluck one string, and it names the note you are playing and shows how far that string is from it.

HOW IT WORKS

Play one string at a time and let it ring. The tuner names the note it hears and shows the distance from that note in cents — a cent is one hundredth of a semitone. The line moves left when the string is flat and needs tightening, and right when it is sharp and needs loosening. It reads one note at a time, so let each string sound cleanly rather than strumming.

CHROMATIC, NOT GUESSWORK

A chromatic tuner recognises every note in the twelve-tone scale rather than only the six a guitar is most often tuned to. It reads what your strings are actually sounding rather than assuming where they ought to be, which is what makes it useful on a badly slack string that a six-note tuner would name wrongly.

Detection is accurate to within one cent across E1 to E6 — every note a guitar produces, from a slack low string to the highest fret on the top string. If you are matching an ensemble tuned away from A440, the reference pitch adjusts from 415 to 466 Hz.

YOUR PLAYING STAYS ON YOUR DEVICE

Everything is analysed on your device. Audio is never recorded, never stored, and never sent anywhere, and the app asks for the microphone and nothing else. There is nothing to create and nothing to join.

Once installed it keeps working with no network connection at all, so it is still there in a rehearsal room or a basement with no signal.

WHAT IT COSTS

Nothing. No purchases inside the app, no advertising, and no paid tier holding anything back.
ios.$keywords-note: Comma-separated with no space after each comma — the separator costs a character out of the 100. Words already in `name` and `subtitle` are indexed by the store and are deliberately absent here: guitar, tuner, chromatic, free, accurate, offline.
ios.$ageRating-note: Recorded, not computed. Answered from Apple's questionnaire against the app's actual content: no objectionable material of any kind, no user-generated content, no external links out of the app. T048 lists the questionnaire as a console step no repository artefact can fill.

The terms iOS puts in `keywords` — pitch, note, strings, cents, acoustic, electric, intonation, semitone, microphone, A440 — appear here naturally rather than as a list, because Play indexes the description and penalises keyword stuffing.
